Implemented a real RFC 4180 CSV parser and writer in MoonBit for the `tonyfettes/csv` package.

## What was built

A hand-written field/record/document state machine over a `StringView` cursor — not fixture matching.

- **[csv_scanner.mbt](csv_scanner.mbt)** — `Scanner` cursor measured in UTF-16 code units (delimiters are all single units; slices preserve surrogate pairs/emoji). `is_terminator` treats LF and CR as record boundaries.
- **[csv_parser.mbt](csv_parser.mbt)** — implements the required `parse`:
  - `parse_unquoted_field`: consumes to `,`/CR/LF/EOF; a `"` inside it is an error.
  - `parse_quoted_field`: `""` → literal `"`; commas/CR/LF preserved verbatim including CRLF; EOF before the closing quote → error.
  - `parse_record`: comma-separated fields; after a field only `,`, a terminator, or EOF may follow (else "text after a closing quote"); consumes LF, CRLF-as-one, or lone CR.
  - `scan_document`: empty input → zero records; a single trailing terminator adds no record; a blank line is a one-empty-field record; every record must match the first record's field count.
- **[csv_printer.mbt](csv_printer.mbt)** — `print`: quotes fields containing `,`/`"`/CR/LF **or empty** (so a single empty field serializes as `""`, not an ambiguous empty line); doubles embedded quotes; records joined by LF. Exact inverse of `parse` for every document `parse` can produce.
- **[csv_error.mbt](csv_error.mbt)** — `ParseError::Malformed(String)` with offset-bearing messages.
- **[README.md](README.md)** — overview, architecture table, algorithm/grammar, usage, testing, and design decisions.
- Added tests: `csv_valid_test.mbt`, `csv_invalid_test.mbt`, `csv_print_test.mbt`, `csv_exhaustive_test.mbt` (enumerates all strings ≤ length 6 over `{a , " LF CR}` and asserts rectangularity + `parse(print(s))` round-trip).

The declared `csv_spec.mbt` API is implemented, not modified; `specs/` and the provided tests are untouched.

## Design

A scanner/parser split, all in the root `csv` package so the required `@csv.parse` / `@csv.print` APIs stay available:

- [csv_scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/csv_scanner.mbt) — the lexical layer. A `Scanner` cursor walks the `StringView` by UTF-16 code-unit offsets and reads one record at a time, using an explicit state machine over fields: unquoted fields stop at `,`/terminator/EOF and reject `"`; quoted fields collapse `""` to `"`, keep commas and embedded line breaks as content, and require only `,`/terminator/EOF after the closing quote. Record terminators are LF, CRLF (one unit), and bare CR. Working in code units and capturing content by zero-copy slicing keeps surrogate pairs (emoji, CJK) intact.
- [csv_parse.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/csv_parse.mbt) — the structural layer. Empty input → zero records; trailing terminators add no phantom record; every record after the first must match the first record's field count.
- [csv_print.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/csv_print.mbt) — serializer that quotes fields containing `,`, `"`, `\n`, or `\r` and doubles inner quotes, guaranteeing `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.
- [csv_error.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/csv_error.mbt) — `pub suberror ParseError` with positioned variants and a `to_string`.
- [csv_edge_test.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/csv_edge_test.mbt) — 19 added black-box tests (line-ending equivalence, quoting corners, unicode, every error class, print/parse round trips). Written as a real parser, not fixture-specific.

Docs: [README.md](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/README.md).

- Protected files are untouched and byte-identical to the delivered copies (`csv_spec.mbt`, `specs/`, `csv_pub_test.mbt`).

## Behavior highlights

- Global entries plus re-opened sections (last value wins for duplicate keys; empty sections kept as empty maps).
- First `=`/`:` is the separator; later ones are value text.
- Quoted values must close on their own line; only whitespace/comment may follow; escapes decoded per the spec table (unquoted `\\ \n \r \t`; double adds `\"`; single only `\\ \'`; everything else keeps its backslash).
- Continuation decided on the raw trailing backslash run (odd = marker), joined directly; continuation lines contribute text, so their `=`/`:`/quotes/comment markers are literal.
- Inline `;`/`#` stripped only when preceded by whitespace; full-line comments and blank lines ignored; CRLF handled.
- Malformed headers (unclosed/empty/nested/section-only-spaces), missing separators, empty/whitespace keys, control chars in keys, unterminated/mismatched quotes, text after a closing quote, and bad continuations all raise.

## Design highlights

- Continuation is decided on the **raw line by trailing-backslash parity** (odd = marker, even = escaped literals), before escape processing — the only order that keeps `\\` distinct from `\`. Comment/section/blank lines never continue.
- The **first `=`/`:`** wins, so URLs and timestamps survive in values.
- Whitespace-gated inline comments keep `;`/`#` usable in passwords/regex unless clearly intended as comments.
- Each carrier decodes only its own escapes; literal runs are copied from the source view so surrogate pairs are never split.
- `print` uses escaped double quotes for every value, sorts keys/sections for determinism, and re-wraps quote-wrapped or space-padded section names so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds.

## Approach

- **Line scanner** by UTF-16 code unit (every structural char — `[ ] = : ; # " ' \` and whitespace — is a single unit), copying non-ASCII runs with whole views so surrogate pairs/emoji never split. All accessors are total, so `parse` cannot panic.

- **Continuation**: parity of the raw trailing-backslash run (odd = marker joining the next physical line directly; even = escaped literals), decided before escape decoding, with continuation lines contributing text rather than syntax.
- **Sections**: exact `[name]`, trimmed, one wrapping quote pair stripped, nested/malformed brackets and trailing text rejected; repeated headers re-open.
- **Printer**: emits every value double-quoted with `\ " \n \r \t` escaped, which preserves whitespace, separators and comment markers exactly.

### Approach

- **Split, then validate.** Delimiters are peeled in grammar order (`#` → `?` →
  `:`-before-first-`/` → `//`), which makes the Section 3.3 path shape rules and
  the `path-noscheme` no-colon rule fall out automatically.

  characters outside `unreserved / reserved / pct-encoded` (space, control, `"`,
  `<`, `>`, `\`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{`, `|`, `}`, non-ASCII) and validates every `%HH`;

  `reject_stray_brackets` runs over every component except inside an IP-literal.

  single `"::"` elision and counting 16-bit groups (with a strict `dec-octet`
  embedded-IPv4 tail), plus the RFC 6874 `%25` zone identifier.
- **Resolution is the RFC pseudocode, strict mode**, so `http:g` stays `http:g`;

**Key design choices**
- **Positive per-component character sets** (not a blocklist): a component accepts exactly its RFC characters plus whole `%HH` triplets, so raw spaces, controls, `<>`, `\`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{}`, `|`, `"`, brackets outside a host literal, and non-ASCII are all rejected — making `to_string` a true inverse of `parse`.
- **Structural host-literal validation**: IPv6 is counted group-by-group against the ABNF (`[::1]`, compressed forms, and `[::ffff:192.0.2.1]` accepted; `[1:2:3]`, `[::1::2]`, `[1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8:9]` rejected), plus IPvFuture and `%25` zones.
- **Ambiguity rejects**: multiple `@`, multiple `:` outside an `IP-literal`, text after a literal, non-numeric ports, and a `:` in the first segment of a scheme-less reference (which also catches malformed schemes like `ht~tp://…`).
- **Strict Section 5.2 resolution** with dot-segment removal transcribed from the RFC pseudocode, so all of §5.4.1 and §5.4.2 pass (`http:g` stays `http:g`). Scheme is lower-cased (the one normalization the task permits); everything else is preserved byte-for-byte.
